newPosts.truncated_body_text: In our first Nano Diaries comic, John brings a scrap of paper to his Hack Club meeting in Córdoba, Spain. He has written three things a volunteer needs to know about a water pickup point. Where is it? How much water is ready? When did someone last check? He wants to see whether those three lines could become a program.

newPosts.subtitle: The MAPLE Nano Card gives young creators a simple place to start. OpenRockets is building a way for their work to stay connected to them as they grow.
newPosts.description: The MAPLE Nano Card gives young creators a simple place to start. OpenRockets is building a way for their work to stay connected to them as they grow.
newPosts.truncated_body_text: Picture a student who writes their first useful program at a school club. A few years later, someone finds it and wants to build on it. What if they could see who made it, find the version they used and understand how they may share it? That is the future we are working toward with MAPLE, the Minor Authors’ Public License for Expression.
